newsitem.title: HUNGARY: World market trends favour TVK's Q1.
newsitem.headline: World market trends favour TVK's Q1.

text.p: Hungarian chemicals company TVK on Monday reported higher sales and net profits for the first quarter of 1997 on the back of declining raw material prices, changes in exchange rates and higher domestic sales.
TVK's IAS net sales rose 39 percent to 19.728 billion forints in the January-March period of 1997, while its net income surged 60 percent to 2.748 billion, the company said in its earnings report.
"In the first quarter of 1997 world market trends were favourable for us," TVK said.

"The average world market price of chemical benzene was some 28 percent above prices in the same period of the previous year, but showed a declining trend," TVK said. "Meanwhile the average world market price of our finished products was some 15 percent higher than in the first quarter of 1996."
The company said that it boosted the proportion of domestic sales to 53 percent from 50 percent, which was in harmony with the company's strategy.
Within TVK's total sales, olefins accounted for 27 percent as against 22 percent in the first quarter of 1996, due to higher price of ethylene and other olefin products, TVK said.
In the January-March months of 1997, polimers accounted for an unchanged 64 percent amid lower capacity use.
Plastics products accounted for 8.5 percent of total sales, down from 11 percent in the same three months of 1996, while the capacity use edged up to 47.4 percent from 45.4 percent.
